final_candidates.decision_summary: Clinically established BRCT-domain mutation that disrupts phosphopeptide-mediated DNA-repair interactions while retaining the folded BRCT scaffold.
RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine mutation strongly associated with loss of BRCA1/BARD1 E3 ligase and tumor-suppressor function.
Another RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine substitution expected to impair BRCA1 function with moderate structural tolerance.

stop_reason.detail: Selected the top three most confident functional-ablation mutations without requiring external tool evidence.

history.rationale: C61 is a zinc-coordinating RING residue; mutation to glycine should disrupt BRCA1 E3 ligase/BARD1-dependent tumor suppressor activity. The alteration is localized to the RING module and is unlikely to broadly disrupt the full-length protein fold.
C61G disrupts the RING zinc-coordination motif and impairs BRCA1-BARD1 E3 ligase activity, a strong loss-of-function event.

C64 forms part of the RING zinc-coordination site, so substitutions here should eliminate ubiquitin ligase and DNA-repair functions. Loss of this cysteine mainly impairs RING activity rather than global folding.
C64G similarly affects RING zinc coordination and is likely to reduce tumor-suppressor function, though slightly less established than C61G.

H41 is a canonical zinc ligand in the RING domain; alanine substitution should ablate E3 ligase function and downstream DNA repair. This targets a key catalytic/structural RING residue while leaving other domains intact.
H41A is a conservative RING-domain perturbation but lower confidence for complete functional ablation.

M1775 sits in the BRCT phosphopeptide-binding pocket; charge-changing substitution to arginine is a well-established loss-of-function mutation for BRCA1-mediated DNA repair. It is expected to impair phospho-ligand recognition with much less effect on overall domain architecture.
M1775R is a well-recognized BRCT-domain pathogenic variant that disrupts phosphopeptide recognition while the BRCT fold is generally retained.

R1699 contributes to BRCT domain interactions and phosphopeptide processing; tryptophan substitution should disrupt BRCA1 repair signaling. This change is strongly linked to pathogenic loss of BRCA1 function.
R1699W is a clinically observed BRCT-domain mutation linked to impaired DNA-repair function.

A1708 is in the BRCT-repeat phospho-binding region; introduction of a charged glutamate should interfere with the phosphopeptide-binding surface and abolish DNA-damage checkpoint signaling, without major whole-protein destabilization.
A1708E is another BRCT-domain substitution that may disrupt protein-protein interactions involved in DNA repair.

P1749 lies in the BRCT interdomain region; arginine substitution should alter the orientation/function of the tandem BRCT repeats and impair BRCA1 tumor suppressor activity. This may preserve fold stability while disrupting functional interactions.
P1749R lies in the BRCT region and may affect folding/function, but confidence is moderated by possible structural destabilization.

S1655 is in the BRCT domain and phosphorylation-dependent interaction network; phenylalanine substitution should disrupt peptide-binding and downstream DNA repair signaling. The mutation is a well-known pathogenic missense variant.
S1655F is less validated and may have milder effects on BRCA1 function.

C27 is part of the RING zinc-coordination cluster; glycine substitution should remove the zinc-binding side chain and impair BRCA1 E3 ligase/tumor suppressor activity. The effect is likely limited to RING-mediated functions.
C27G affects a RING cysteine but has lower clinical/functional evidence than C61G/C64G.

C47 is another conserved RING zinc ligand; substitution to glycine should disrupt the RING E3 ligase surface and abolish DNA-repair function. This avoids targeting residues outside the local RING fold.
C47G may disrupt zinc binding but is the least confidently tied to strong loss of function among current candidates.
